BAY PROCEDURE Tacoma RV Center · Document Library CONCERN Furrion FACT12SA2 rooftop shows E3 MODEL Furrion FACT12SA2 DATE 2026-10-09 WO# - PRIMARY Furrion Chill FACR CCD-0008666, pages 15 and 18. VISUAL FLOWCHART FACT12 shows E3. Is 12 V present on the data connector? Repair the 12 V feed or the data line. Is the data connector seated? Seat the connector and retest the code. Is the freeze sensor on the coil? Sensor is seated and E3 remains. Write the readings and stop. Reseat the freeze sensor on the evaporator coil. Retest the code. YES NO YES NO YES NO BAY PROCEDURE Bay order · Tacoma RV Center WHAT THIS PATTERN USUALLY MEANS A FACT12 E3 is a communication fault. Measure 12 V and the data line at the connector before any board swap. Then confirm the freeze sensor is seated on the evaporator coil. BAY ORDER (DO THIS FIRST) Step 1: Measure 12 V at the control box Where: At the control box, on the red 12 VDC cable and the black ground cable. Tools: Multimeter on DC volts. Do this: 1. Find the red 12 VDC cable and the black ground cable. 2. Measure the voltage between them. Good looks like: About 12 V DC. Bad looks like: No 12 V at the cable. Next: If it is good, check the thermostat cable connection. If it is bad, repair the 12 V feed and retest the code. Step 2: Check the thermostat cable connection Safety: Disconnect power at the battery disconnect or fuse first. Where: At the control box, on the four cables tagged To wall thermostat. Do this: 1. Match each cable color to its wall thermostat wire. 2. Look for a pushed-back pin. 3. Look for a loose connector. Good looks like: Each color matches and every pin is seated. Bad looks like: A crossed color, a pushed-back pin, or a loose connector. Next: If it is good, check the freeze sensor on the evaporator coil. If it is bad, repair the connection and retest the code. Step 3: Check the freeze sensor on the evaporator coil Do this: 1. If it is loose or off the coil, reseat it and retest. 2. If it is already seated and E3 remains, write the readings and stop. DO NOT - Do not replace the control board before the 12 V, data line, and connector checks.
